Analyze an augmented row-column design

Source: R/augmented_row_column.R
analyze_augmented_row_column_design.Rd

Fits the fixed-effects model: y = mean + rowgroup + colgroup + rowgroup:colgroup + rowgroup:row + colgroup:col + genotype + error. Sums of squares are sequential, in the order above. Degrees of freedom are the ranks actually estimable from the observed (non-missing) plots. For a complete design they equal the augmented row-column formulas, reported in anova_df, which use field rows (k), field columns (s), row groups (gk), column groups (gs), check cultivars (vc), and unreplicated entries (ve): row groups gk - 1, rows within row groups k - gk, column groups gs - 1, columns within column groups s - gs, blocks (gk - 1)(gs - 1), genotypes vc + ve - 1, and error as the remainder of k * s - 1.

Usage

analyze_augmented_row_column_design(
  data,
  response,
  genotype_col = "all_entries",
  rowgroup_col = "rowgroup",
  colgroup_col = "colgroup",
  row_col = "row",
  col_col = "col",
  type_col = "type",
  control_col = "is_control",
  random_blocks = FALSE,
  entries = c("fixed", "random"),
  spatial = FALSE,
  spatial_nseg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A complete augmented row-column design data frame, usually design$design from augmented_row_column_design(), with a response column added.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

genotype_col

Name of the genotype/treatment column.

rowgroup_col

Name of the row-group column.

colgroup_col

Name of the column-group column.

row_col

Name of the field row column.

col_col

Name of the field column column.

type_col

Optional entry type column. Used only for genotype summaries.

control_col

Optional control flag column. Identifies the checks for entries = "random"; otherwise used only for genotype summaries.

random_blocks

Logical. If TRUE, rows within row groups, columns within column groups and blocks are random effects, which recovers inter-block information (Wolfinger et al., 1997; Möhring et al., 2015). Row and column groups stay fixed. Fitted by REML with 'lme4'.

entries

"fixed" (default) or "random". With "random", checks are fixed and the unreplicated entries are random effects from a common breeding population (Piepho, Williams and Fleck, 2006); entry values are then BLUPs. Fitted by REML with 'lme4'.

spatial

Logical. If TRUE, the plot errors get a spatial add-on: a two-dimensional P-spline surface over rows and columns fitted with the 'SpATS' package, with row and column groups fixed and rows, columns and blocks random. Genotypes are fixed.

spatial_nseg

Optional number of P-spline segments for columns and rows, c(col, row). Defaults to half the number of columns and rows (at least 3, at most 40).

Value

An object of class augmented_row_column_analysis: a list with

input, formula, model

The column mapping, model formula, and an lm fit on the check plots.

anova, anova_df, anova_formatted

Sequential ANOVA (estimable df), design df formulas, and a formatted ANOVA table.

plot_results

The input data with fitted values and residuals.

genotype_summary

One row per genotype with raw, fitted, and adjusted means and the standard error of the adjusted mean.

adjusted_means

Genotypes ranked by adjusted mean (best first).

diagnostics

Error df, residual standard deviation, R-squared, mean_sed (mean standard error of a difference between two adjusted means), lsd_5pct (the matching least significant difference), and flags for rank deficiency or a saturated fit.

variance_components, mixed_model

For mixed or spatial fits: the REML variance components and the lmerMod or SpATS fit; otherwise NULL.

message

A note when F-tests or adjusted means are not estimable.

Details

Unreplicated entries each fit their own plot exactly, so the model is fitted without a dense genotype design matrix: the residual comes from the replicated (check) plots alone. model is the corresponding lm fit on the check plots, with aliased columns removed. This keeps the analysis fast for large trials.

Mixed and spatial models

The ANOVA table always comes from the fixed-effects model of Piepho and Williams (2016, Eq. 1). With random_blocks, entries = "random" or spatial, the adjusted means, their standard errors, mean_sed and lsd_5pct come from the corresponding REML fit instead. Standard errors are exact prediction standard errors from the mixed-model equations for the estimated variance components; lsd_5pct uses the fixed-model error df as an approximation.

Adjusted means

With the default fixed-effects model, genotype effects are fixed, so the adjusted means are best linear unbiased estimates (BLUEs). Each is the genotype effect plus the average row, column, and block effect over all observed plots, i.e. the expected value of the genotype in an average plot of the field. For an unreplicated entry this is its observed value corrected for the row, column, and block effects of its plot, estimated from the checks; its standard error combines the plot error and the uncertainty of that correction. Use adjusted_mean (not raw_mean) to rank and select entries.

Examples

design <- augmented_row_column_design(
  treatments = paste0("G", seq_len(108)),
  controls = paste0("Check", seq_len(4)),
  rows_in_field = 12,
  cols_in_field = 12,
  rows_per_block = 4,
  cols_per_block = 4,
  n_candidates = 3,
  seed = 123
)

design_data <- design$design
design_data$yield <- rnorm(nrow(design_data), mean = 100, sd = 10)
analysis <- analyze_augmented_row_column_design(design_data, response = "yield")
analysis
